answers: Lane: objective (signals, ownership, and what the contracts permit). Readings 1 and 8 are read costs, reading 6 is a window, reading 7 is row shape, and readings 2 to 5 are budgets. Reading 2 is a test timeout over waits that each end on a signal. Reading 3 has two layers: COMPONENT_WAIT ceilings plus the table timeout. Reading 4 is a ceiling on `waitForAnimations`, which parks on `finished`. Reading 5 is a settle predicate with a loop cap. The rulings give each one's property, signal, and sizing. One sizing rule applies to every budget: the slowest duration measured across the six named one-holder runs, times a margin. The margin is the larger of the band ratio (618.6/494.0) and the test's own max/min spread. Test timeouts add one inner ceiling on top, so a stalled inner wait reports its named condition before Vitest's timeout. Readings taken under lane M load break the host-queue rule and size nothing.

No. A 5 ms window with one frame is right only after the engine's bounce has ended, and the observer starts before that. A refused Escape on the static dialog runs `#prevent` (src/browser/Modal.ts:232-257). It emits `hidePrevented` (:233), adds `modal-static` in the same task (:244), focuses the host (:248; no attribute write), and waits a padded timer that runs even under reduced motion because `animated` is forced to true (:247; helpers.ts:935-945). It then removes `modal-static` (:251), waits a second pad (:252), and restores inline overflow-y (:254). It writes no `aria-*`, and the trap writes no attributes (Trap.ts:75-86). The late class removal is the mutation that failed jb2b-1 on `Open the static dialog through escape:shown` (runs/jb2b-1/journey/light-1280.txt:456). The engine has no completion event for the bounce, so the observer cannot wait on one. The act must instead wait for the class/style flip that the engine tests already treat as the settle (Modal.test.ts:464-470), and the window then observes. A refusal window remains a clock by nature, because absence has no event; its 5 ms term is the engine's pad contract (helpers.ts:939). Alternative: an engine completion event. Refused: the engine reproduces Bootstrap's wire events (constants.ts:93-99), and the DOM already carries the end.

The previous state's panel is not the source. `buildJourney` destroys the showcase and the journey engine in the same task (tests/setupBrowser.ts:1417-1424 → :1398-1404 → :1494-1500; Veneer.ts:115-125), and Tip.destroy removes the panel immediately (Tip.ts:279, :289). The comment at :3663 belongs to `buildComponent`, not `buildJourney`. The light tooltip state also follows `closed`, which starts no engine. The stray is therefore a panel created in the same iteration that has not been disposed yet. The signal is the panel's disconnection: `#disposePanel` (Tip.ts:284-292) is the only path, and the `panel` getter turns undefined there. `hidden.bs.tooltip` (Tip.ts:324) and `phase === 'hidden'` (:127-135) can both hold while the panel stays connected (:318-322), so neither proves it gone. Wait before the count (:1317) until the body's direct `.tooltip`/`.popover` children are only the bound panel. Do not wait before `buildJourney` (already synchronous), and do not count only owned elements: that redefines `excluded` and would hide a leaked panel. `excluded` stays in the row. It is a count, the J-B2 pair agree on it (10763), and moving it would change every preservation row string, which the compare refuses against every baseline (compare.ts:526-528).

Yes, each table gets its own bound, but derived rather than stored. The bound is the table's own `scenarios.length` × a measured per-row cost × margin + COMPONENT_WAIT. Do not add it as a COMPONENT_TABLES property: a stored per-table figure drifts whenever rows change (AGENTS.md design law, 'Derive state'), and 30-odd figures would each need re-measuring on every landing. `it.each` takes one timeout, so registration moves to a loop, with titles byte-identical as the gate. The popover table blocks sizing. Motion=true read 69.6 to 165.8 s across the six runs against 10.8 to 13.3 s at motion=false, and that one table accounts for most of reading 8's band. The U2 probe must explain it before any bound absorbs it.

Yes. Pass COMPONENT_WAIT at tests/setupBrowser.ts:4445, :5078, and :5180. These waits park on `finished`, so the ceiling lengthens only the report of a missing signal and never a passing row. Margin property, two-sided. The floor is the slowest measured settle × 618.6/494.0; with >1000.5 ms on the transform transition (completion-b3-journey-after-3b), the floor is about 1.25 s. The ceiling must stay below each table's bound minus its measured duration, so the named animation failure reports before Vitest's timeout. 5000 ms sits inside both limits. The comment at :3199 must name the run behind 774.5 ms. The library default stays: the call-site `WaitOptions` already exists (index.d.ts:3161).

Neither. The 8-poll predicate is a 70 to 80 ms clock (10 ms interval, core index.js:241, :251) that cannot tell a late-starting scroll from a finished one. The 100-press cap is a figure chosen by eye. Wait on the scroller's `scrollend` through `waitForEvent` (core index.d.ts:804), subscribed before the press, but only when a geometry precheck shows the key can move the scroller. Then wait two frames for the engine's IntersectionObserver callback (Scrollspy.ts:52, :114-130). Let the boundary end the loop. `activate.bs.scrollspy` (Scrollspy.ts:167) fires only when the active link changes, so it cannot end a per-press wait. It stays the act's check (tests/setupBrowser.ts:5719).

All seven changes are veneer test-layer: U3 to U7, plus the U1 instrument under tmp/. `@orkestrel/test/browser` needs no change: `waitForAnimations` and `waitForCondition` take `WaitOptions` per call, and `waitForEvent` exists. Leave its 1000 ms default to its owner. The engine needs no stage B addition for these readings. A tip 'hidden' lifecycle already exists (`hidden.bs.tooltip`/`hidden.bs.popover`, constants.ts:155, :162; Tip.ts:324), and the DOM carries the precise end (panel disconnection, `panel` getter :141-143). The modal bounce ends on an observable class/style flip. Stage B work arises only if the U2 probe traces the popover excess into engine code. Records to amend: (a) brief reading 7: `buildJourney` mounts fresh and destroys the prior engine; the tip exposes `panel` and emits `hidden`, not only `phase`. (b) brief reading 8: most of the band is the popover motion=true table. (c) tests/setupBrowser.ts:3199: name the run behind 774.5 ms and add the 1000.5 ms after-3b reading.
risks: Tension (Orchestrator): readings 1 to 3 were taken under lane M load, which breaks the rule that every Chromium or CPU-loading command goes through the host queue. This design sizes nothing from them and does not cover that load.

Tension (stage B / subjective lane): the tip `phase` getter reads 'hidden' while the panel stays connected when an active or hovered trigger holds it (src/browser/Tip.ts:318-323). This matches Bootstrap's `complete()` branches. Whether it is a defect is stage B's ruling; U6 does not depend on it.
Tension (subjective lane): the names of the exported modal-settle predicate (U3), the scroll helper (U5), and the per-row cost constants (U7) are open.

Refusal: a non-Bootstrap completion event for the modal bounce or a tip 'disposed' event. The engine mirrors Bootstrap's wire events (src/browser/constants.ts:93-99, :148-165), the DOM already carries both ends, and AGENTS.md § Design laws 'Minimal public API' says to 'Create or substantively expand a capability with its first real consumer'. A test-only consumer of an engine event the DOM already exposes does not meet that law.

Refusal: moving `excluded` to a Journal count. A count-only entry with no `seconds`/`milliseconds` joins the gated Journal (compare.ts:220-239, :536-547), and changing the row string breaks row equality with every baseline (compare.ts:526-528). Either way a re-baseline would be forced.
Risk: U7 changes registration from `it.each` to a loop. Any change to a title breaks the host-bound title gate (compare.ts:161-193, :555-559). The byte-identical title criterion is load-bearing.

Risk: U5 assumes Chromium 141 fires `scrollend` on an element scroller for a keyboard scroll, both instant and animated, and delivers the IntersectionObserver callback within two frames. If either fails, the `scrollend` wait reports a named timeout and does not pass silently. The filtered scrollspy runs are the check.
Risk: U5 starts `waitForEvent` before `pressKeys`. A press that throws leaves a pending rejection unless it is handled.
Risk: U6's wait may time out because hover holds a panel (Tip.ts:322) and nothing then disposes it. That is a real finding, not a reason to park the pointer before the count.

Measurement missing: no one-holder integration-project reading for the witness test (reading 1). No run is named for the 774.5 ms settle (tests/setupBrowser.ts:3199). No per-row or per-wait timing explains popover motion=true at 69.6 to 165.8 s against 10.8 to 13.3 s at motion=false; U2 supplies it.
